rule.title: Ordinance No. 7,992-N.S. amending Berkeley Municipal Code Chapter 13.63 – Prohibition on the Sale or Use of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms to Set Rents or Manage Occupancy Levels for Residential Dwelling Units
rule.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license or provide to Berkeley landlords a coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels, and unlawful for landlords to use one when setting rents or occupancy for residential units. Each month and each unit is a separate violation; the City Attorney and aggrieved tenants may sue.
rule.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rule.penalty: Civil action by City Attorney or tenant for damages, injunctive relief, restitution of illegal profits and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, plus mandatory attorney's fees to the prevailing City Attorney or tenant.
rule.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code Chapter 13.63; Ordinance No. 7,992-N.S.
rule.status_basis: Ordinance amends existing BMC Chapter 13.63, so the chapter is already law; the document shows it was passed to print on November 18, 2025, and final adoption date is not shown.

coverage.summary: Applies to coordinated pricing algorithms used or sold for residential dwelling units in Berkeley.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Excludes aggregated anonymous rental data reports, affordable-housing rent/income limit tools, and market research, appraisal or software development uses.

rule.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley 
landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. 
B. It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.

rule.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rule.requirement: Rental housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection or other decisions, including refusing to rent, demanding higher deposits or rent, or refusing to add family members. rule.title: M.G.L. c. 186, § 18 – Reprisal for reporting violations of law or for tenant's union activity
rule.requirement: Landlords and their agents may not threaten or take reprisals against tenants for enforcing housing laws, reporting code violations, or organizing or joining a tenants' union. A notice of termination (other than for nonpayment), rent increase, or substantial alteration of tenancy terms within six months of such activity is presumed to be a reprisal, rebuttable only by clear and convincing evidence.

rule.title: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B (limits on upfront charges by lessors)

rule.title: General Laws Chapter 186, Section 31 - Notice to quit for nonpayment of rent
rule.requirement: A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent must be accompanied by a form documenting repayment agreements and giving information on rental assistance programs, court rules and orders, and federal or state eviction restrictions, with a prominent statement that the notice is not an eviction. rule.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rule.requirement: Residential rental property owners may not use algorithmic revenue management software that collects or processes competitors' nonpublic leasing information to set or recommend rents. Software providers and other coordinators may not use such software to facilitate agreements or coordinate pricing among competing residential landlords. The attorney general must set up a complaint portal, and existing remedies under the New Jersey Antitrust Act are preserved.
rule.penalty: Existing remedies under the New Jersey Antitrust Act are preserved; no specific penalty stated.

rule.quoted_span: The FAIR Act prohibits residential rental property owners from using algorithmic revenue management software that collects or processes competitors' nonpublic leasing information to set or recommend rental prices.

rule.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
rule.requirement: Housing providers may not ask about an applicant's criminal record until after a conditional offer. They may never consider arrests without conviction, expunged, pardoned, vacated, juvenile or sealed records. After an offer they may consider only listed serious convictions or recent convictions within look-back periods, and must do an individualized assessment and give written reasons if they withdraw the offer.

rule.penalty: Civil penalty up to $1,000 (first violation), $5,000 (one prior violation in 5 years), $10,000 (two or more prior violations in 7 years); possible return of application fee and up to $1,000 paid to applicant

rule.requirement: A landlord may evict only on the statutory grounds, such as nonpayment, disorderly conduct, property damage, lease violations, health and safety violations, permanent retirement of the property, condominium conversion, owner occupancy and certain criminal offenses. Each ground carries its own Notice to Quit period, ranging from 3 days to 3 years. Relocation assistance is required for some grounds.

rule.requirement: Tenants may be removed only by court order on listed good causes. In owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings the landlord must prove one of the specified causes, with notice to quit of 3 months (at will or year-to-year), 1 month (month-to-month) or 3 days (disorderly, destructive or rule violations). Landlords who evict to occupy the unit must occupy it for 6 months, and landlords who evict to retire the building must keep it out of residential use for 5 years.
